fact: Apollo 11 landed the first humans on the Moon, fulfilling a decade-long space race goal. The Woodstock festival in upstate New York became a defining symbol of counterculture and peace.

Intel released the 4004, the world's first commercially available microprocessor, laying groundwork for modern computing. Greenpeace was founded in Vancouver, launching a new era of environmental activism.
Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen, setting the stage for the personal computer revolution. The Vietnam War officially ended with the fall of Saigon in April.
Apple Computer was officially incorporated, formalizing the company that would reshape personal technology. Star Wars redefined blockbuster filmmaking and merchandising for generations to come.

fact: CNN launched as the first 24-hour cable news network, transforming how the world consumed news. John Lennon was assassinated in New York City, shocking fans worldwide.
Apple introduced the Macintosh, popularizing the graphical user interface for everyday consumers. AT&T's breakup took effect, reshaping the American telecommunications industry.
The Live Aid benefit concerts raised massive global awareness and funds for famine relief in Ethiopia. Nintendo released the NES in North America, reviving the home video game industry.
The Berlin Wall fell, symbolizing the collapse of Communist rule across Eastern Europe. Tim Berners-Lee proposed the concept that would become the World Wide Web.
The Soviet Union officially dissolved, ending the Cold War era. The World Wide Web became publicly available, opening the internet to broader use.
Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as South Africa's first Black president, marking the end of apartheid. Jeff Bezos founded Amazon, initially as an online bookstore.
Princess Diana died in a car crash in Paris, prompting an outpouring of global mourning. J.K. Rowling published the first Harry Potter novel, beginning a publishing phenomenon.
Napster launched, disrupting the music industry through peer-to-peer file sharing. Worldwide anxiety peaked over the Y2K bug as computers approached the new millennium.

fact: The September 11 terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon reshaped global politics and security. Wikipedia launched, eventually becoming the world's largest collaborative encyclopedia.
